result:
I found 10 rules in `pricebook.py` whose results didn't match their docstrings, and fixed them all. Afterwards I re-ran a check that compares every rule against its docstring and the shared rules at the top of the file, and all 150 rules now match.

**Rules that gave different results:**

| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 35 | The cap was applied to the price before the discount, not to the discount | Cap the discount at 30,000 won |
| 93 | Same problem | Cap the discount at 30,000 won |
| 102 | Same problem | Cap the discount at 50,000 won |
| 45 | Used `round()` (rounds to nearest) | Round down to the won (`//`) |
| 57 | Same problem | Round down to the won (`//`) |
| 115 | Same problem | Round down to the won (`//`) |
| 66 | Discount was 3%, docstring says 2% | Changed to 2% |
| 83 | Discount was 8%, docstring says 7% | Changed to 7% |
| 105 | Documented as marginal but discounted every unit | Discount only the units above the threshold: `(qty - 30) * unit` |
| 107 | Documented as whole but discounted only the units above the threshold | Discount every unit: `base` |

**Rules with no change in results:** rules 39 and 43 checked `qty >= 6` and `qty >= 21`, but the docstrings say 5 and 20. Under the marginal formula, the discount is 0 when the quantity is exactly at the threshold, so prices were already correct. I changed them to 5 and 20 anyway so the code matches the docstrings.

I didn't touch the docstrings or any other rules.

STATUS: DONE
